name: Daryl Maciel
life: “I still remember a skate wheel rolling loose in our kitchen.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Daryl by a small Friday habit. Daryl takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I promised to fix the wheel and gave the mirror my son's old skate bearing.
appearance: Daryl has a long plait tucked inside the collar, a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a washed violet jersey. It usually goes with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. When somebody else has the floor, Daryl touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Daryl is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To fit the skate bearing to the cracked wheel.
family: Alfred Ross is Daryl’s second cousin. Daryl makes the call. Alfred is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The day sailor's divorce*, Alfred says, “I am the new partner everyone resents. I would like Sunday morning alone on shore anyway.”
connections: Merritt Levi. The last purchase receipt stays in the same envelope as the new wheel bearing.

reactions.situation: The mirror owner wants it back during a fitting
reactions.response: Daryl asks the two shops for enough time to finish the fitting in privacy.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Daryl writes down their exact words with room left for uncertainty and gives them back to check.

reactions.response: Daryl helps set the table, then takes a short turn outside alone.
